titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§87–92: The Pale Geldings and Bo'orchu
about: Six sections, one recovery. §87 is Sorqan-Shira's farewell to Temüjin, with the mare, the cooked lamb, the buckets and the bow and two arrows (no saddle, no flint). §88 is Temüjin's finding of his family up the Kimurqa. §89 is their life by the Blue Lake, living on marmots and field-mice. §90 is the theft of the eight pale geldings, Belgütei's return too late, Temüjin's three-night tracking, and the meeting with the young man who gives his name as Bo'orchu, who rides in with him and drives the geldings out. §91 is the pursuit, the exchange of arrows and the fall of night. §92 is the three-day ride and Bo'orchu's refusal of any share. The grammar to watch is the converb chain (-žu / -žü / -ču / -ġed, Ming 着, 'having … -ing'), the speech-introducing ügülerün and speech-closing keġen / keġebe, the reflexive-possessive (-ben / -jan / -jen, 'one's own'), and the reciprocal -ldu- ('at one another', 'together'). The hard places, flagged in the notes, are the 'ash-scraping' sentence at the head of §87, the alurγai-bar 'swept track' of §§88 and 90, the geġü saγan aqu-ji phrase of §90, the nada-ača of §91, and the önžē line near the end of §92.

sentences.t: Nüṅčiġül-i oduγsan-u qoina Sorγan-Šira ügülerün:
sentences.l: Searchers (acc.) having-gone's after, Sorγan-Šira saying:
sentences.i: After the searchers had gone away, Sorqan-Shira said:
sentences.n: §87 opens with a sentence that is not quite clear: Nüṅčiġül-i is Ming 搜的行, 'the searching (ones)', with the accusative -i, and oduγsan-u is od- 'go' + the past participle -uγsan + the genitive -u, Ming 去了的, so 'of the having-gone'; with qoina 'after' it gives 'after the searchers had gone'. The searchers are Taichi'ud men looking for Temüžin; the exact case relation is my reading. ügülerün (說) is ügüle- 'speak' + the converb -rün, and introduces a speech, as it will all through this part.

morph.gloss: searcher, search (Ming 搜的 'the searching'; stem uncertain) [搜的 行]

sentences.t: "Nama-ji hünesü-ġer keisgen aldaba.
sentences.l: Me (acc.), ash-like, scraping-off, has-slipped-away.
sentences.i: "You have slipped away from me, as ash is scraped off."
sentences.n: The hardest line of the opening. The Ming gives 我行 'me', 灰般 'like ash', 刮 'scrape', 脫了 'slipped off'. Nama-ji is 'me' with -ji; hünesü-ġer is hünesü 'ash' + the instrumental -ġer, Ming 般 'like'; keisgen is Ming 刮 and I cannot name its stem; aldaba is alda- 'slip away' + the past -ba. The sense I give, that the man (Temüžin, "you" in my English; the Mongol line has no subject) escaped from the speaker as ash comes off a scraping, fits the Ming but is not certain. Shiratori's full stop closes the sentence.

morph.gloss: instrumental: like, as (Ming 般 'like'; form uncertain)
scraping, scraped off (Ming 刮 'scrape'; stem and ending uncertain) [刮]

sentences.t: Edöġe eke-ben deġü-ner(i)-jen erin od" keġežü
sentences.l: Now mother-his-own, younger-brothers (acc.)-his-own, seeking, go!" saying,
sentences.i: Now go and look for your mother and your brothers," he said, and
sentences.n: eke-ben is eke 'mother' + the reflexive-possessive -ben (Ming 自的行), 'one's own mother', here 'your own' because it follows the imperative; deġü-ner(i)-jen is deġü 'younger brother' + plural -ner + the accusative -i (Shiratori's bracket) + the reflexive -jen. erin is eri- 'seek' + the converb -n, and od is the bare stem of od- 'go' used as an imperative. keġežü (說着) closes the quotation and, being a converb, hands the sentence on to what Sorqan-Shira did next.

sentences.t: aman čaγaγ̇an eremüg qulaγči- n-i unuγ̇ulžu tel-quriγan bolγažu
sentences.l: Mouth white barren dun (acc.), making-ride, two-mothers'-milk lamb, making-done-through,
sentences.i: He had him mount a white-muzzled, barren dun mare, and he cooked through a lamb that had fed on two ewes' milk,
sentences.n: A converb chain broken into three units (§87's gifts). aman čaγaγ̇an eremüg qulaγči-n-i is a run of Ming glosses 口白不生駒的甘草黃 ('mouth, white, non-foaling, liquorice-yellow') read as one horse: a white-muzzled (or white-mouthed) dun mare that bears no foal. qulaγči- and n-i are one word, qulaγčin + the accusative -i, which Shiratori splits in two. unuγ̇ulžu is unu- 'ride' + the causative -γ̇ul- + -žu, 'making (him) ride'. tel-quriγan (喫二母乳的羔兒) is a lamb that sucked two mothers; bolγažu is bol- 'become' + the causative -γa- + -žu, and the Ming 煮熟着 gives the sense 'cooked through'. Both readings are mine, from the Ming.

morph.gloss: barren, not bearing foals (Ming 不生駒的; of a mare; form uncertain) [不生駒的]
dun, liquorice-yellow (Ming 甘草黃; a horse colour; Shiratori cuts the word before n-i) [甘草黃]
accusative (the n belongs to qulaγčin; Shiratori prints n-i) [行]
lamb that has fed on two mothers' milk (Ming 喫二母乳的羔兒; compound uncertain) [喫二母乳的羔兒]
to become, to be cooked through (Ming 煮熟着) [煮︀熟着]

sentences.t: köġür nambuγa žasažu emeġel ülü ögün kete ülü ögün
sentences.l: Small-skin-bucket, large-skin-bucket, preparing, saddle not giving, flint not giving,
sentences.i: he made ready a small and a large skin bucket, but gave no saddle and no flint,
sentences.n: köġür (小皮桶) and nambuγa (大皮桶) are the small and the large skin bucket. žasažu is žasa- 'prepare' + -žu. Then ülü ögün twice: ülü 'not' + ög- 'give' + a converb ending (-ün, form uncertain), Ming 不與, 'not giving'; the negation stands before the verb. emeġel is the saddle (鞍子) and kete the fire-striker (火鎌), so Sorqan-Shira withheld both.

morph.gloss: to prepare, set in order [整治着]
fire-steel, flint-striker (Ming 火鎌 'fire sickle') [火鎌]

sentences.t: numu ögčü qojar sumu ögbe.
sentences.l: Bow giving, two arrows gave.
sentences.i: but he gave a bow and two arrows.
sentences.n: ögčü is ög- 'give' + the converb -čü, and ögbe the past form. qojar 'two' stands before the thing counted, qojar sumu, 'two arrows' (Ming 兩隻 箭), the order of number and noun in this part. Shiratori's full stop closes the sentence.

sentences.t: Tedüi žasažu ilebe.
sentences.l: So preparing, sent.
sentences.i: So he equipped him and sent him off.
sentences.n: Tedüi 'that much, so' (Ming 那些, 'those') sums up the gifts, and žasažu 'preparing' takes them up again. ilebe is ile- 'send' + the past -be; the Ming 敎去了 reads 'made (him) go', hence 'sent him off'.

morph.gloss: that much, so much, so (Ming 那些 'those, that many') [那些]
to prepare, set in order [整治着]

sentences.t: Temüžin tein oduγ̇ad šibeġeležü qorγolaγsan γažar-tur(i)-jan kürčü
sentences.l: Temüžin, so having-gone, hedge-making stockade-made place-in-his-own, arriving,
sentences.i: So Temüjin went, and he reached his own place, which had been hedged and made into a stockade,
sentences.n: §88 begins another converb chain, cut at the natural joints. oduγ̇ad is od- 'go' + the converb -uγad; šibeġeležü is šibeġe 'hedge, fence' (藩籬) + the verb-maker -le- + -žü; qorγolaγsan is qorγo 'stockade' (寨) + -la- + the participle -γsan, 'having been made into a stockade'. γažar-tur(i)-jan is γažar 'land' + the dative-locative -tur + the reflexive -jan, 'in one's own place'; the (i) is Shiratori's. Whose stockade this is, and why it is called his own, I cannot say from the Ming alone: it is probably the family's old camp. kürčü is kür- 'arrive' + -čü.

morph.gloss: hedge, fence (Ming 藩籬) [藩籬把着]
land, place [地面 裏自的行]

sentences.t: ebesün-ü alurγai-bar Onan müren öġede möčkižü
sentences.l: Grass's swept-track-by, Onan river upstream, tracking,
sentences.i: and, following the swept track in the grass, tracing the trail up the Onan river,
sentences.n: ebesün-ü is ebesün 'grass' + the genitive -ü, 'of the grass'. alurγai-bar is the puzzle: Ming 掃道依着, 'following the sweeping-road', and -bar is the instrumental, so 'by, along' it. I take alurγai as a track or lane swept clear (by passing horses or people) through the grass; that is a guess from the Ming. Onan müren öġede (逆着 'against') is 'up the Onan river'. möčkižü is möčki- 'track' (踏蹤着, stem inferred) + -žü.

morph.gloss: swept track (Ming 掃道, 'sweeping the road'; sense uncertain) [掃道 依着]
the Onon, a river (Ming 河名) [河名]
to track, follow the trail (Ming 踏蹤着; stem inferred) [踏蹤着]

sentences.t: hörönēče Kimurqa γoroqan oro- žu iren ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: From-the-west Kimurqa brook entering, coming, was.
sentences.i: from the west he entered the Kimurqa brook and came on.
sentences.n: hörönēče is Ming 西自, 'from the west'; I read hörön as 'west' with the ablative -ēče, but the stem is uncertain. Kimurqa is the name of a stream (水名) and γoroqan 'brook'. oro- and žu are printed apart by Shiratori; together they are oro- 'enter' + the converb -žu (入着). iren is ire- 'come' + -n, and ažuγ̇u is a- 'be' + the past -žuγu (有來), so 'was coming, came on'. Shiratori's full stop closes the sentence.

morph.gloss: west, the west side (Ming 西; stem uncertain) [西自]
Kimurqa, a stream (Ming 水名) [水名]
converb: -ing (Shiratori sets it off as a separate word) [着]
past: there was, he was (Ming 有來)

sentences.t: Tere öġede möčkiġed Kimurqa γoroqan-(n)u Beder qošiγ̇un-u qorčuqui boldaγ-a büküi-dür žoluγalduba.
sentences.l: That upstream, having-tracked, Kimurqa brook's Beder's beak-of, Qorčuqui lone-hill-at being-when, met-one-another.
sentences.i: Going up the same way, tracking the trail, they met each other, at the Qorchuqui lone hill by the spur of Beder on the Kimurqa brook.
sentences.n: The meeting. qošiγ̇un-u is qošiγun 'beak' (觜, so 'spur' or 'point' of a hill) + the genitive; Beder (山名) and Qorčuqui (山名) are both named in the Ming as mountains, and boldaγ-a is boldaγ 'lone hill' (孤山) + the dative-locative -a. büküi-dür is bü- 'be' + the participle -küi + -dür, 'at the being', Ming 有的時分 'when (they) were'. žoluγalduba is žolu- 'meet' + a reciprocal (-γaldu-, 相 'one another'; I cannot say how the pieces divide) + the past -ba. The subject is not named; from §89 the ones who meet are Temüžin and his family.

morph.gloss: that, that one; also he, she [那]
to track, follow the trail (Ming 踏蹤着; stem inferred) [踏蹤着]
Kimurqa, a stream (Ming 水名) [水名]
Beder, a mountain (Ming 山名) [山名]
Qorčuqui, a name (Ming 山名) [山名]
reciprocal: one another (Ming 相; split uncertain)

sentences.t: Tende neisüldüžü odču Burqan-Qaldun-u ebüre Kürelkü dotora
sentences.l: There joining-together going, Burqan-Qaldun's front, Kürelkü within,
sentences.i: There they joined together and went on, to the front of Burqan Qaldun, within the Kürelkü,
sentences.n: §89 opens, the family now reunited. neisüldüžü (相合着, 'joining together') has a reciprocal ending after the stem neisü-; the exact division -l-dü- is uncertain. Burqan-Qaldun-u is the mountain's name + the genitive; ebüre 'in front' (前) is the postposition after Burqan-Qaldun-u, and dotora 'within' the postposition after Kürelkü, another mountain name (Ming 山名).

morph.gloss: to join together, unite (Ming 相合) [相合着]
Burqan Qaldun, a mountain (Ming 山名) [山名 山的]
in front, before (ebür + -e; Ming 前) [前]
Kürelkü, a mountain (Ming 山名) [山名]

sentences.t: Seṅgür γoroqan-u Qara-Žirügen-ü kökö naγ̇ur nutuγlažu
sentences.l: Seṅgür brook's Qara-Žirügen's blue lake, camping,
sentences.i: and camped at the Blue Lake of Qara-Jirügen on the Sengür brook,
sentences.n: Two genitives stack up before the noun: Seṅgür γoroqan-u (the Sengür brook's) and Qara-Žirügen-ü (Ming 山名, a mountain's), both governing kökö naγ̇ur, 'blue lake' (靑, 海子). The way the two names relate to the lake is my reading. nutuγlažu is nutuγla- 'camp, occupy as pasture' + -žu.

morph.gloss: Sengür, a stream (Ming 水名) [水名]
Qara-Jirügen, a mountain (Ming 山名) [山名的]
to camp, take as pasture [營盤做着]

sentences.t: aqui-dur tarbaγad küčügür alažu iden büleġe.
sentences.l: Living-when, marmots field-mice killing, eating, used-to-be.
sentences.i: and while they lived there they killed marmots and field-mice and ate them.
sentences.n: aqui-dur is a- 'dwell' (住) + the participle -qui + -dür, 'at the dwelling', so 'while living'. tarbaγad is tarbaγan 'marmot' (土撥鼠) with the plural -d; küčügür is Ming 野鼠, 'wild rat', here 'field-mouse' (the reading is not certain). alažu iden is a pair of converbs, ala- 'kill' + -žu and ide- 'eat' + -n, then büleġe, 'used to be' (有來), which turns the whole into a habit: this is how they lived.

morph.gloss: field-mouse, wild rat (Ming 野鼠; reading uncertain) [野鼠]
past: there was, used to be (Ming 有來)

sentences.t: nigen üdür širγa aγta-tan naiman morid ger-ün dergede baižu büküi-ji
sentences.l: One day pale geldings eight horses tent's beside standing-being (acc.),
sentences.i: One day eight pale geldings were standing beside the tent,
sentences.n: §90 opens with a participle phrase that is picked up by the next unit. aγta-tan is aγta 'gelding' (騸馬) + -tan, Ming 等 'and the like'; the ending is uncertain. naiman morid is 'eight horses' (八箇 馬每), the count before the thing counted, and morid is morin + the plural -d. büküi-ji is bü- 'be' + -küi + the accusative -ji; the accusative shows that this phrase is the object of the seeing that follows.

sentences.t: deġerme irežü üžetele deġermedčü jorčiba.
sentences.l: Robbers coming, when-looking, robbing, set-out.
sentences.i: robbers came, saw them, robbed them and made off.
sentences.n: deġerme is Ming 劫賊, 'robber', and deġermedčü (劫着) a verb made from it, 'robbing'. üžetele is üže- 'see' + -tele, Ming 看着; I read it as 'on seeing'; the accusative büküi-ji in the unit before names what they saw. jorčiba is jorči- 'set out' (stem inferred from the Ming 去) + the past -ba. Shiratori's full stop closes this long sentence.

morph.gloss: while, until, as soon as (Ming 着; sense uncertain)
to rob (from deġerme; Ming 劫着; stem inferred) [劫着]
to set out, go (stem inferred from Ming 去) [去了]

sentences.t: Jabuγad üžežü qočorba.
sentences.l: Walking, seeing, fell-behind.
sentences.i: Those on foot saw it and were left behind.
sentences.n: jabuγad is jabu- 'walk, go on foot' + -γad; Ming 步行每 puts the plural 每 on it, so 'those who were on foot' (the ending is uncertain, either a converb or a plural). üžežü is üže- 'see' + -žü. qočorba is qočor- 'fall behind' (stem inferred from Ming 落後) + the past -ba. The sense is that the men without horses could not follow.

morph.gloss: to walk, go on foot (Ming 步行) [步行每]
to fall behind (Ming 落後; stem inferred) [落後了]

sentences.t: Belgütei darγi oqodur qoṅγor-i unužu tarbaγačilara odču büleġe.
sentences.l: Belgütei, bald-tail dun (acc.) riding, marmot-hunting going, used-to-be.
sentences.i: Belgütei had gone off riding the dun with the docked tail to hunt marmots.
sentences.n: Belgütei is away: unužu is unu- 'ride' + -žu, qoṅγor-i is Ming 甘草黄馬, a dun or bay horse, in the accusative. darγi oqodur (Ming (禿) (尾), 'bald' and 'tail') I take as a horse's name or description, 'docked-tail'; that is uncertain. tarbaγačilara is tarbaγan 'marmot' + a hunter-verb (-či-la-, Ming 捕 'catch') + an ending -ra, which I read as a purpose converb, 'in order to hunt marmots'; the endings are uncertain. odču büleġe is converb + past of habit, 'had gone'.

morph.gloss: bald, docked (Ming (禿); of a horse's tail; sense uncertain) [(禿)]
tail, short tail (Ming (尾); with darγi, 'bald-tail'; sense uncertain) [(尾)]
bay or dun, yellowish-brown (Ming 甘草黄馬; a horse colour) [甘草黄馬(行)]
verb: to hunt (-či 'one who', -la- 'make'; Ming 捕; split uncertain)
converb of purpose: in order to (form uncertain)
past: there was, used to be (Ming 有來)

sentences.t: Üdeši naran singegsen-ü qoina Belgütei dargi oqodur qoṅγor-tur tarbaγad ačižu niγsaqalžatala jabuγan kötölžü irebe.
sentences.l: Evening, sun set-of after, Belgütei, bald-tail dun-on marmots loaded, swaying, walking leading, came.
sentences.i: In the evening, after the sun had set, Belgütei came back on foot, leading the dun on which marmots were loaded, swaying under them.
sentences.n: üdeši naran singegsen-ü qoina is 'evening, after the sun's having set': singegsen-ü is singe- 'set, sink' (Ming 落, stem inferred) + the participle -gsen + the genitive -ü, with qoina 'after'. qoṅγor-tur is the dun with the dative-locative 'on'; ačižu is ači- 'carry as a load' + -žu. niγsaqalžatala (顫動着, 'shaking') is a stem niγsaqal- + an ending I do not know, -žatala (perhaps -tala 'while'); the sense is that the load swayed, a guess from the Ming. jabuγan kötölžü is 'on foot, leading'; irebe is ire- 'come' + -be.

morph.gloss: to set, sink (Ming 落; stem inferred) [落了的]
bald, docked (Ming (禿); of a horse's tail; sense uncertain) [(禿)]
tail, short tail (Ming (尾); with darγi, 'bald-tail'; sense uncertain) [尾]
bay or dun, yellowish-brown (Ming 黃馬 'yellow horse'; a horse colour) [黃馬 行]
to carry as a load [駄着]
to sway, wobble (Ming 顫動着; stem uncertain) [顫動着]
to walk, go on foot [步行]

sentences.t: Širγa aγta-tan-i deġerme abču odba.
sentences.l: Pale geldings (acc.) robbers taking, went.
sentences.i: Robbers had taken the pale geldings and gone.
sentences.n: Shiratori's full stop sets this off as the news given to Belgütei. aγta-tan-i is the geldings with the accusative -i, the object of abču, ab- 'take' + -ču; odba is od- 'go' + -ba. The subject deġerme precedes the verb, as usual.

sentences.t: kēġesü Belgütei ügülerün:
sentences.l: When-they-said, Belgütei saying:
sentences.i: When they told him, Belgütei said:
sentences.n: kēġesü is keġe- 'say' + the conditional converb -ġesü (Ming 說呵, 'when told'), written with a long ē because the stem vowel and ending have run together. It is the first of several -sü forms in this part; read it as 'when (it) was said'. Belgütei ügülerün: opens a speech.

morph.gloss: conditional converb: when, if (written kēġesü, the stem vowel run together; Ming 說呵)

sentences.t: "Bi nekesü" keġebe.
sentences.l: "I let-me-pursue" said.
sentences.i: "Let me give chase," he said.
sentences.n: bi 'I'. nekesü is neke- 'pursue' (the Ming 襲去 means 'go and raid, attack') + the optative -sü, 'let me …', the same ending as in ögsü and bolsu below. keġebe is keġe- 'say' + the past -be and closes the quotation.

morph.gloss: to pursue, give chase (Ming 襲去 'go and raid') [襲去]

sentences.t: Qasar ügülerün: "Či ülü čidaqu; bi nekesü" keġebe.
sentences.l: Qasar saying: "You not able; I let-me-pursue" said.
sentences.i: Qasar said, "You cannot do it; I will give chase."
sentences.n: Qasar speaks next. či 'you' (你) and ülü čidaqu: ülü 'not' + čida- 'be able' (Ming 能) + the participle -qu, so 'you are not able'. Shiratori's semicolon marks the turn to bi nekesü, 'let me pursue'. The same two-clause shape returns in Temüžin's speech.

morph.gloss: to pursue, give chase (Ming 襲去 'go and raid') [襲去]

sentences.t: Temüžin ügülerün: "Ta ülü čidaqu; bi nekesü" keġežü
sentences.l: Temüžin saying: "You not able; I let-me-pursue" saying,
sentences.i: Temüjin said, "You cannot do it; I will give chase,"
sentences.n: Temüžin speaks. ta 'you' (the plural polite form, Ming 您, as opposed to či) is courteous to the older Belgütei, or to the pair of them. The closing converb is keġežü, 'saying', not keġebe, so the sentence runs on into what Temüžin did.

morph.gloss: to pursue, give chase (Ming 襲去 'go and raid') [襲去]

sentences.t: dargi qoṅγor-i Temüžin unužu Širγa aγta-tan-i ebesün-ü alurγai-bar möčkižü γurban qonožu
sentences.l: Bald-tail dun (acc.) Temüžin riding, pale geldings (acc.) grass's swept-track-by tracking, three spending-the-night,
sentences.i: Temüjin mounted the docked-tailed dun, tracked the pale geldings along the swept track in the grass, and spent three nights,
sentences.n: The chain begins with unužu 'riding' and the dun in the accusative (dargi here, darγi above; the spelling varies). ebesün-ü alurγai-bar möčkižü repeats the track-following phrase of §88, with the same guess that alurγai is a swept lane in the grass. qonožu is qono- 'spend the night' + -žu, so three nights pass on the trail.

morph.gloss: bald, docked (Ming (禿); of a horse's tail; sense uncertain) [(禿)]
bay or dun, yellowish-brown (Ming 黃馬 'yellow horse'; a horse colour) [黃馬行]
swept track (Ming 掃道, 'sweeping the road'; sense uncertain) [掃道 (依着)]
to track, follow the trail (Ming 踏蹤着; stem inferred) [踏蹤着]
to spend the night (stem inferred) [宿着]

sentences.t: manaγar erte mör-tür olon oduγ̇un-dur nigen gürümele köġün küġün geġü saγ̇an aqu-ji žolγažu
sentences.l: Next-morning early track-on, many herd-among, one brisk lad man mare milking being (acc.), meeting,
sentences.i: Early on the next morning, on the track, among a large herd of horses, he met a lively young man who was milking mares,
sentences.n: manaγar (清, 'clear') is 'the next morning', with erte 'early'. mör-tür is mör 'track' + the dative-locative -tür, 'on the track'; oduγ̇un-dur is Ming 馬羣 裏 'among the herd of horses' (the stem oduγun is uncertain). The man: gürümele is Ming 爽利 'brisk', köġün 'young man' (後生) and küġün 'man'. geġü saγ̇an aqu-ji is Ming 課馬 擠 有的行: geġü is 'mare, one levied for milking' (the reading is uncertain), saγan is saγa- 'milk' + -n, and aqu-ji is a- 'be' + -qu + the accusative -ji. The accusative marks the milker as the object of žolγažu 'meeting'.

morph.gloss: tomorrow, the next morning (Ming 淸 'clear, early') [淸]
herd of horses (Ming 馬羣; stem uncertain) [馬羣 裏]
brisk, lively (Ming 爽利; form uncertain) [爽利]
son; also lad, young man (Ming 後生 'junior') [後生]
mare kept for milking (Ming 課馬 'levy-horse'; reading uncertain) [課馬]

sentences.t: širγa aγta-tan-i surabasu tere köġün ügülerün:
sentences.l: Pale geldings (acc.) if-asked, that lad saying:
sentences.i: When he asked about the pale geldings, the young man said:
sentences.n: surabasu is sura- 'ask' + the conditional converb -basu (Ming 挨問呵), 'if/when (one) asks'. The one who asks is Temüžin, not named in this unit. The accusative aγta-tan-i makes the geldings the thing asked about. tere köġün ügülerün: introduces the answer.

morph.gloss: conditional converb: if, when (Ming 挨問呵)
that, that one; also he, she [那]
son; also lad, young man (Ming 後生 'junior') [後生]

sentences.t: "Ene manaγar naran urγuqu-jin urida širγa aγta-tan naiman morid eġü-ber hüldežü jorčiba.
sentences.l: "This morning sun rising-of before, pale geldings eight horses this-way driving, set-out.
sentences.i: "This morning, before sunrise, eight pale geldings went by this way, being driven off.
sentences.n: ene manaγar (淸早, 'early morning') naran urγuqu-jin urida is 'this morning, before the sun's rising': urγuqu-jin is urγu- 'rise' (Ming 出) + the participle -qu + the genitive -jin, with urida 'before'. eġü-ber is Ming 這裏行, 'this way' (eġü is uncertain) + the instrumental -ber, 'by, along'. hüldežü jorčiba is 'driving, they set out'; the driver is not named, but is plainly the robbers. Shiratori's full stop closes the sentence.

morph.gloss: tomorrow, the next morning; here this morning (Ming 淸早) [淸早]
this way, here (Ming 這裏; stem uncertain) [這裏 行]
to chase, drive (stem inferred from Ming 趕) [趕着]
to set out, go (stem inferred from Ming 去) [去了]

sentences.t: Mör in-ü bi žaγ̇ažu ögsü" kēġed
sentences.l: Track their I pointing-out, let-me-give," having-said,
sentences.i: I will point out their tracks to you," he said, and
sentences.n: mör in-ü is 'their track' (the genitive in-ü stands after its noun). žaγ̇ažu is žaγ̇a- 'tell, point out' (吿着) + -žu, and ögsü is ög- 'give' + -sü, 'let me give' (與呵). So 'I will give (you) the pointing-out', that is, 'I will show you'. kēġed closes the quotation with a converb.

morph.gloss: his, her, their (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to tell, point out (Ming 吿) [吿着]
optative: let me give (Ming 與呵)

sentences.t: oqodur qoṅγor-i talbiγ̇ulžu Temüžin-(n)e oroγ šiṅqula-ji unuγ̇ulba.
sentences.l: Docked-tail dun (acc.) making-let-loose, Temüžin-to black-back white-horse (acc.) made-ride.
sentences.i: and he let the docked-tailed dun go free and set Temüjin on a black-backed white horse.
sentences.n: talbiγ̇ulžu is talbi- 'let go' + the causative -γ̇ul- + -žu (敎放着), 'having it let loose'. Temüžin-(n)e is the dative-locative 'to Temüžin' (Ming 行). oroγ šiṅqula-ji is Ming 黑脊 白馬 行, 'black-spined white horse' with the accusative -ji; šiṅqula is a word I know only from the Ming gloss. unuγ̇ulba is unu- + the causative -γ̇ul- + the past -ba, 'made ride'. The speaker, now the host, changes Temüžin's horse.

morph.gloss: tail, short tail (Ming (尾); with darγi, 'bald-tail'; sense uncertain) [禿尾]
bay or dun, yellowish-brown (Ming 黃馬 'yellow horse'; a horse colour) [黄馬 行]
to let go, set loose [敎放着]
Temüjin, a man's name [人名 行]
white horse (Ming 白馬; stem uncertain) [白馬 行]

sentences.t: Mün öġesün qurdun qubi-ji unuba.
sentences.l: Himself swift light-yellow-horse (acc.) rode.
sentences.i: He himself rode a swift pale-yellow horse.
sentences.n: mün öġesün is '(he) himself' (Ming 本 自己; mün is the emphatic particle). qurdun is 'swift' (快). qubi-ji is Ming 淡黃馬 行, a pale-yellow horse with the accusative; qubi is uncertain as a stem. unuba is unu- 'ride' + the past -ba. Shiratori's full stop closes it.

morph.gloss: light-yellow horse (Ming 淡黃馬; stem uncertain) [淡黃馬行]

sentences.t: Ger-tür(i)-jen ba ülü odun nambuγa saγ̇uluγa-ban keġer-e buγužu talbiba.
sentences.l: Home-to-his-own even not going, large-skin-bucket, skin-pail-his-own, open-ground-on, covering, let-go.
sentences.i: Without even going home, he covered his big skin bucket and his skin pail, left out on the open ground, and let them be.
sentences.n: Ger-tür(i)-jen is ger 'home' + the dative-locative -tür + the reflexive -jen, 'to one's own home'. ba is 'even, also', and ülü odun is the negated converb 'not going'. nambuγa (皮桶) and saγ̇uluγa-ban (皮斗, + the reflexive -ban 'his own') are two skin vessels, and keġer-e is 'on the open ground'. buγužu is Ming 葢着, 'covering', stem inferred. The picture is a man who leaves his household things behind to help a stranger; the exact action (covering them over) is my reading of the Ming.

morph.gloss: skin pail, milk-pail (Ming 皮斗) [皮斗 自(的)行]
open ground, steppe (Ming 野地) [野地行]
to cover (Ming 葢着; stem inferred) [葢着]
to let go, set loose [放了]

sentences.t: Nökör či bürün maši muṅtanižu aisu ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Friend, you being, greatly in-hardship, came was.
sentences.i: "Friend, you have come into great hardship.
sentences.n: Quoted speech, with no opening quotation mark in Shiratori. nökör is 'companion, friend'. či bürün is či 'you' + bü- 'be' + the converb -rün, Ming 呵, which I take as an 'as for' marker: 'as for you, being what you are'. muṅtanižu is muṅtana- 'be in hardship' (艱難着, stem inferred from muṅ 'hardship') + -žu. aisu ažuγ̇u pairs aisu 'come' with a- + -žuγu, 'was/had come'.

morph.gloss: to be in hardship (Ming 艱難着; stem inferred) [艱難︀着]
to come (stem; the ending is unclear, Ming 來 'come') [來]

sentences.t: Ere-jin muṅ nigen bi že.
sentences.l: Man's hardship one is, indeed.
sentences.i: A man's hardship is all one.
sentences.n: ere-jin is ere 'man' (男子) + the genitive -jin. muṅ is 'hardship' and nigen 'one'; bi (有) is 'is' here, not 'I' (the Ming gloss shows the difference), and že is the particle 也者, 'so, indeed'. The line reads like a proverb; the sense 'we all suffer the same' is my reading of the Ming 一箇.

morph.gloss: man, male (Ming 男子) [男子 的]
particle, so, indeed (Ming 也者) [也者︀]

sentences.t: Bi čima-dur nököčesü.
sentences.l: I you-to let-me-be-companion.
sentences.i: I will be your companion.
sentences.n: Bi čima-dur is bi 'I' + čima- (the oblique stem of či 'you') + the dative-locative -dur, 'to you'. nököčesü is nököče- 'be a companion' (做伴, formed from nökör) + the optative -sü, 'let me / I will'.

morph.gloss: you (oblique stem of či) [你 行]
to be a companion (Ming 做伴; stem inferred from nökör) [做伴]

sentences.t: Ečige min-u Naqu-Bajan keġegdejü.
sentences.l: Father my Naqu-Bajan being-called.
sentences.i: My father is called Naqu Bayan.
sentences.n: Ečige min-u: the genitive min-u ('of me') stands after its noun, as in-ü does. keġegdejü is keġe- 'say' + a passive (-gde-) + the present -jü, so 'is said, is called' (Ming 呼的有).

morph.gloss: my (genitive of bi, placed after its noun) [我的]
Naqu Bayan, a man's name [人名]
present: is (Ming 呼的有, 'is called'; split uncertain)

sentences.t: Bi γaγča köġün in-ü bi Boγ̇orču neretü bi" keġeġed
sentences.l: I only son his I, Boγ̇orču name-having am," having-said,
sentences.i: I am his only son, and my name is Bo'orchu," he said, and
sentences.n: The first words of the answer: Bi γaγča köġün in-ü bi is 'I am his only son' (köġün in-ü, 'son of him', with bi 'I am' closing the clause). neretü is nere 'name' + the possessive -tü, 'having the name', the possessive pattern met earlier. This is where the young man gives his name; he is the Boγ̇orču who will serve Temüžin for the rest of the work. The quotation closes at bi", and keġeġed is keġe- + the converb -ġed.

morph.gloss: his, her, their (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]

sentences.t: širγa aγta-tan-u mör(i)-jer in-ü möčkižü γurban qonožu
sentences.l: Pale geldings' track-along his tracking, three spending-the-night,
sentences.i: Following the pale geldings' track, they tracked on and spent three nights,
sentences.n: The chain resumes after the speech: širγa aγta-tan-u is 'of the pale geldings' (the genitive -u), mör(i)-jer is mör 'track' + -jer, an ending with the shape of the instrumental (Ming 蹤跡依着 'following the track'), as in §86. in-ü stands after, 'their'. möčkižü is 'tracking' and qonožu 'spending the night'. The subject is not named; the unit before is Boγ̇orču's speech, and Temüžin's "Friend, you stay here" a few units on shows the two riding together, so I read 'they'.

morph.gloss: instrumental: along, by (Ming 蹤跡依着, 'following the track'; the (i) is Shiratori's)
his, her, their (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to track, follow the trail (Ming 踏着; stem inferred) [踏着]
to spend the night (stem inferred) [宿着]

sentences.t: üdeši naran quburi tašin büküi-dür nigen kürijen irgen-dür kürbe.
sentences.l: Evening, sun ridge patting being-when, one ring-camp people-among reached.
sentences.i: At evening, when the sun was just touching the ridge, they reached a ring-shaped camp, among the people.
sentences.n: tašin (拍着, 'patting, slapping') is a converb whose stem I can only infer; the picture is probably the sun resting on the ridge, but I am not sure. büküi-dür is 'when being'. kürijen (圈子, 'circle') names a ring-camp, a circle of tents; irgen-dür is 'among the people' (百姓), with the dative-locative -dür. kürbe is kür- 'reach' + the past -be.

morph.gloss: to strike, pat (Ming 拍着; stem inferred, sense uncertain) [拍着]
ring of tents, circle camp (Ming 圈子 'circle') [圈子]

sentences.t: širγa aγta-tan naiman morid tere jeke kürijien-ü kižaγ̇ar-a ebesülen baižu büküi-ji užebe.
sentences.l: Pale geldings eight horses, that big ring-camp's edge-at, grazing standing being (acc.), saw.
sentences.i: They saw the eight pale geldings standing, grazing, at the edge of that great camp-ring.
sentences.n: The same eight pale geldings, now found. kürijien-ü is kürijen + the genitive (Shiratori spells it with an extra i); kižaγ̇ar-a is kižaγar 'edge' (邊) + the dative-locative -a. ebesülen (喫草, 'eating grass') I read as ebesün 'grass' + a verb-maker + the converb -n. baižu büküi-ji is 'standing, being (acc.)'. užebe is üže- 'see' + -be, spelled with u.

morph.gloss: that, that one; also he, she [那]
ring of tents, circle camp [圈子 的]
grazing, eating grass (ebesün 'grass' + -le- verb-maker + -n converb; Ming 喫草; split uncertain) [喫草]

sentences.t: Temüžin ügülerün: "Nökör či ende bai;
sentences.l: Temüžin saying: "Friend you here stand;
sentences.i: Temüjin said, "Friend, you stay here;
sentences.n: bai in the Ming is 立 'stand', here an imperative (bare stem): 'stay'. ende is 'here'. Shiratori's semicolon ends the first clause of the instruction.

morph.gloss: to stand, stay (bare stem, imperative; Ming 立) [立]

sentences.t: bi. širγa aγta-tan tede bi; hüldežü γarsuγai" keġebe.
sentences.l: I. Pale geldings those are; driving, let-come-out" said.
sentences.i: I will go. Those are the pale geldings; I will drive them out," he said.
sentences.n: bi. stands alone, with the verb of going understood ('I [shall go]'). tede is 'those' (那的每); bi (有) is 'are'. γarsuγai is γar- 'go out' + -suγai, Ming 出來; I read it as an optative, 'let them come out', and hüldežü 'driving' as the means: 'I will bring them out by driving'. The ending is uncertain. keġebe closes the quotation.

morph.gloss: to chase, drive (stem inferred from Ming 趕) [趕着]
optative: let … (Ming 出來; form uncertain)

sentences.t: Boγ̇orču ügülerün: "Nököčesü keġen ireleġe; bi ende jakin baiqu" kēġed
sentences.l: Boγ̇orču saying: "Let-me-be-companion saying, came; I here why stand," having-said,
sentences.i: Bo'orchu said, "I came saying, 'I will be your companion'; why should I stand here?"
sentences.n: Boγ̇orču's refusal to wait. nököčesü keġen is the earlier 'I will be your companion' as a quotation (keġen closes it, 麽道). ireleġe is ire- 'come' + -leġe, Ming 來了 'came' (the ending is uncertain; elsewhere -leġe is a past). jakin is 'how, why' (爲甚), and baiqu is bai- 'stand' + the participle -qu, 'to stand', here a rhetorical question. kēġed is the converb 'having said'.

morph.gloss: to be a companion (Ming 做伴; stem inferred from nökör) [做伴]
past: came (Ming 來了; form uncertain)

sentences.t: qamtu dobtulžu oroγ̇ad širγa aγta-tan-i hüldežü γarba.
sentences.l: Together galloping, having-entered, pale geldings (acc.) driving, went-out.
sentences.i: and together they galloped in, drove out the pale geldings and came away.
sentences.n: qamtu is 'together'. dobtulžu is Ming 走馬着, 'galloping', with a stem I do not know. oroγ̇ad is oro- 'enter' + -γad. The last two are 'driving' (hüldežü) and γarba (γar- 'go out' + -ba), 'came out'. The unit ends §90.

morph.gloss: to gallop (Ming 走馬着; stem uncertain) [走馬着]
to chase, drive (stem inferred from Ming 趕) [趕着]

sentences.t: qoināča haran ubur subur nekežü aisu.
sentences.l: From-behind people one-after-another pursuing, came.
sentences.i: From behind, men came in pursuit, one after another.
sentences.n: §91 opens with the chase. qoināča is qoina 'behind' + -ča, the short form of the ablative -ača, 'from behind'. haran (人每) is 'people'. ubur subur is Ming 陸續, a Chinese word meaning 'one after another', and I take the Mongol pair as an echo word of the same sense (uncertain). nekežü is neke- 'pursue' (stem inferred) + -žü; aisu is 'came'.

morph.gloss: one after another (with subur, Ming 陸續 'in succession'; sense uncertain) [陸]
one after another (with ubur, Ming 陸續; sense uncertain) [續]
to pursue (stem inferred from Ming 襲着) [襲着]
to come (stem; the ending is unclear, Ming 來了 'came') [來了]

sentences.t: Nigen čaγaγ̇an moritu küġün uγ̇urγa barižu γaγčaγ̇ar güičežü aisu.
sentences.l: One white horse-having man, lasso-pole holding, alone, catching-up, came.
sentences.i: One man on a white horse, holding a lasso-pole, caught up with them alone.
sentences.n: moritu is mori (morin 'horse') + the possessive -tü, 'horse-having', the possessive pattern again. uγ̇urγa is a lasso-pole (套馬竿). γaγčaγ̇ar is γaγča 'single' + the instrumental -γar, Ming 獨自, 'by himself'. güičežü is Ming 趕上着 'catching up', stem inferred.

morph.gloss: to catch up with (Ming 趕上; stem inferred) [趕上着]
to come (stem; the ending is unclear, Ming 來了 'came') [來了]

sentences.t: Boγ̇orču ügülerün: "Nökör numu sumu nada-ača bi qarbulaldusu" keġebe.
sentences.l: Boγ̇orču saying: "Friend bow arrow from-me, I let-me-trade-shots," said.
sentences.i: Bo'orchu said, "Friend, the bow and arrows: give them here; I will shoot it out with him."
sentences.n: The hard word is nada-ača: na- (the oblique stem of bi) + the dative-locative -da + the ablative -ača, 'from me'; the Ming gives 我行 將來, 'bring (it) from me'. I do not know whether Boγ̇orču wants Temüžin to hand him the bow and arrows, or means 'from my side'; the translation leaves it open and keeps the Ming's sense of 'give them here'. qarbulaldusu is qarbula- 'shoot' (stem inferred) + the reciprocal -ldu- (厮 'each other') + the optative -su, 'let me trade shots'.

morph.gloss: me (oblique stem of bi) [我行 將來]
ablative: from (Ming 我行 將來; sense uncertain)
to shoot (Ming 射; stem inferred) [厮射]
reciprocal: at one another (Ming 厮 'each other')

sentences.t: Temüžin ügülerün: "Min-u tula či erüsteġüžei; bi. qarbulaldusu" keġežü
sentences.l: Temüžin saying: "My on-account you may-be-harmed; I let-me-shoot-it-out" saying,
sentences.i: Temüjin said, "You might be harmed on my account; I will shoot it out myself,"
sentences.n: min-u tula is 'on account of me': the genitive min-u + tula (上頭). erüsteġüžei (Ming 恐被害, 'lest he be harmed') is erüste- 'be harmed' + an ending -ġüžei, which I read as 'lest' (precative; the shape is uncertain). Temüžin refuses to let Boγ̇orču take the risk.

morph.gloss: my (genitive of bi, placed after its noun) [我的]
because of, on account of [上頭]
to be harmed (Ming 被害; stem inferred) [恐被害]
precative: lest, may it not … (Ming 恐 'for fear that'; shape uncertain)
to shoot (Ming 射; stem inferred) [厮射]
reciprocal: at one another (Ming 厮 'each other')

sentences.t: esergü qarin qarbulalduba.
sentences.l: Facing, back, shot-at-one-another.
sentences.i: He turned back to face them, and they traded shots.
sentences.n: esergü is Ming 迎着 'to meet', 'facing'; qarin (囘去) 'back'. qarbulalduba is the same verb as in the speech above, now with the past -ba: the arrows are shot. The sense 'turned back to face' combines esergü and qarin and is my reading.

morph.gloss: facing, against (Ming 迎着 'to meet') [迎着]

sentences.t: Tere čaγaγ̇an moritu küġün uγ̇urγa-bar(i)-jan dokižu baiba.
sentences.l: That white horse-having man, lasso-pole-his-own, pointing, stood.
sentences.i: The man on the white horse stopped, motioning with his own lasso-pole.
sentences.n: uγ̇urγa-bar(i)-jan is uγ̇urγa 'lasso-pole' + the instrumental -bar (Ming 敎, 'with, by means of') + the reflexive -jan, 'his own'. dokižu is Ming 指點着, 'pointing, gesturing' (stem inferred), baiba is bai- 'stand' + -ba. The exact picture, a man holding the others back with his pole, is my reading.

morph.gloss: that, that one; also he, she [那]
instrumental: with, by means of (Ming 敎)
to point, gesture (Ming 指點着; stem inferred) [指點着]

sentences.t: Qoitus nököd güičežü irebe.
sentences.l: Rear-ones companions, catching-up, came.
sentences.i: The companions who had been behind caught up and came.
sentences.n: qoitus is qoitu 'behind, the rear' (後頭的) + the plural -s, and nököd is nökör 'companion' with -d (伴當每); both are plural, the Ming 每 confirming it. güičežü 'catching up' and irebe 'came' are the chain and the end.

morph.gloss: behind, the rear (Ming 後頭的) [後頭的每]
to catch up with (Ming 趕上; stem inferred) [趕上着]

sentences.t: Naran šiṅgežü odba.
sentences.l: Sun setting, went.
sentences.i: The sun went down.
sentences.n: šiṅgežü is Ming 落着, 'setting, sinking' (stem inferred), and odba is od- 'go' + -ba. The chain is short: a converb + a past.

morph.gloss: to set, sink (Ming 落着; stem inferred) [落着]

sentences.t: Duġušin bolžu aisu.
sentences.l: Dusk becoming, came.
sentences.i: Dusk came on.
sentences.n: duġušin is Ming 黃昏 'dusk'. bolžu is bol- 'become' + -žu, aisu 'came'. Shiratori ends the sentence with a full stop.

morph.gloss: to come (stem; the ending is unclear, Ming 來了 'came') [來了]

sentences.t: Qoitu tede haran baruγ̇an boldažu baižu qočorba.
sentences.l: Rear those people dark being-overtaken, standing, fell-behind.
sentences.i: The pursuers at the rear were caught by the dark, halted and fell behind.
sentences.n: qoitu tede haran is 'the rear, those people' (後頭的 那的每 人每). baruγ̇an (黑了, 'blackened') is 'dark'. boldažu is Ming 被黑做着, 'made dark, overtaken by the dark'; I read bolda- as a passive of bol- (stem uncertain). baižu qočorba is 'stood and fell behind': they halted.

morph.gloss: dark, darkness (Ming 黑了; stem uncertain) [黑了]
to be overtaken, be made (Ming 被黑做着; passive; stem uncertain) [被黑做着]
to fall behind (Ming 落後; stem inferred) [落後了]

sentences.t: Tere süni düliġed γurban üdür γurban süni düližü kürbe.
sentences.l: That night riding-through, three days three nights riding-through, arrived.
sentences.i: They rode through that night, and for three days and three nights rode on without stopping, and arrived.
sentences.n: §92 opens with the long ride. düliġed and düližü are Ming 兼行, 'travelling double', that is by night as well as day; the stem düli- is my inference. The two converbs are -ġed 'having …' and -žü '-ing'. γurban üdür γurban süni is 'three days, three nights' (the count precedes the noun). kürbe is kür- + the past -be. The subject is not named; it is Temüžin and Boγ̇orču.

morph.gloss: that, that one; also he, she [那]
to ride day and night (Ming 兼行; stem inferred) [兼行了]
to ride day and night (Ming 兼行; stem inferred) [兼行着]

sentences.t: Temüžin ügülerün: "Nökör bi čima-dāča aṅgida ede morid(i)-jan abqu-u büleġe;
sentences.l: Temüžin saying: "Friend, I you-from apart these horses-my-own taking? was;
sentences.i: Temüjin said, "Friend, apart from you, was I to have taken these horses of mine?
sentences.n: čima-dāča is čima- (the oblique stem of či) + the ablative -dāča (Ming 自), a long form; aṅgida is Ming 外, 'apart, besides', so 'apart from you'. morid(i)-jan is morin + the plural -d + the accusative (i) (Shiratori's) + the reflexive -jan, 'my own horses'. abqu-u büleġe is ab- 'take' + the participle -qu + the question -u (Ming 麽) + büleġe 'was': a rhetorical question, 'would I have taken them without you?' The reading is my own from the Ming.

morph.gloss: ablative: from (long form of -da-ača; Ming 自)

sentences.t: qubijalduja; kėdüi-ji abqu keġemü" keġebe.
sentences.l: Let-us-divide; how-many (acc.) take, say?" said.
sentences.i: Let us share them; how many will you take?" he said.
sentences.n: qubijalduja is qubi- (a stem inferred from Ming 分 'divide') + a reciprocal (-jaldu-) + -ja (咱, 'let us'), 'let us divide among ourselves'; the division of the ending is uncertain. kėdüi-ji is 'how many' with the accusative, and keġemü is keġe- 'say' + the present -mü, '(you) say' (the person is not marked; I read an offer, 'how many will you take?').

morph.gloss: to share out, divide (Ming 分; stem inferred) [分咱]
how many (Ming 幾多) [幾多 行]

sentences.t: Boγ̇orču ügülerün: "Bi sain nökör-i čima-ji muṅtanižu aisu keġen
sentences.l: Boγ̇orču saying: "I good friend (acc.) you (acc.) in-hardship came saying,
sentences.i: Bo'orchu said, "I said, 'My good friend, you have come into hardship,'
sentences.n: The accusatives sain nökör-i and čima-ji both look at muṅtanižu aisu, '(who) have come in hardship': the whole clause is what the speaker said (keġen, 麽道) to himself. The accusative is the Ming's own pointer (行), and the construction, with its two objects, is loose; my English smooths it.

morph.gloss: to be in hardship (Ming 艱難着; stem inferred) [艱難︀着]
to come (stem; the ending is unclear, Ming 來了 'came') [來了]

sentences.t: sain nökör-e tusa bolsu keġen nököčežü irebe bi.
sentences.l: Good friend-to use let-me-be saying, companion-being came I.
sentences.i: and, saying, 'Let me be of use to a good friend,' I came to be your companion.
sentences.n: nökör-e is nökör + the dative-locative -e, 'to a friend' (Ming 行). tusa (濟) is 'use, help'. bolsu is bol- + the optative -su, 'let me be'. nököčežü is nököče- 'be a companion' + -žü. irebe bi is 'I came'.

morph.gloss: to be a companion (stem inferred from nökör) [做伴着]

sentences.t: Önžē-ü keġežü abqu bi.
sentences.l: Extra-wealth saying, take I.
sentences.i: Should I take it, calling it extra wealth?
sentences.n: önžē-ü is Ming 外財, 'outside wealth', that is gain from outside; I read it as 'extra goods, outside gain' with the genitive -ü (uncertain). keġežü is 'saying'. abqu bi (要 我) 'I take'. The Ming does not show a question, but the following lines, in which Boγ̇orču says he will not take anything, make a rhetorical question the likeliest sense. The line is one of the doubtful ones of the part.

morph.gloss: extra goods, outside wealth (Ming 外財; sense uncertain) [外財]

sentences.t: Ečige min-u Naqu-Bajan neretü bijü.
sentences.l: Father my Naqu-Bajan name-having is.
sentences.i: My father is named Naqu Bayan.
sentences.n: neretü is nere 'name' + the possessive -tü, 'named'. bijü is bü- 'be' + the present -jü, 'there is, is' (有). Shiratori's full stop closes the sentence.

morph.gloss: my (genitive of bi, placed after its noun) [我的]
Naqu Bayan, a man's name [人名]

sentences.t: Naqu-Bajan-(n)u γaγča köġün in-ü bi bijü.
sentences.l: Naqu-Bajan's only son his I am.
sentences.i: I am the only son of Naqu Bayan.
sentences.n: Naqu-Bajan-(n)u is the name + the genitive; the (n) is Shiratori's. köġün in-ü bi bijü is 'son of him, I am', the same turn as in §90.

morph.gloss: Naqu Bayan, a man's name [人名]
son; also lad, young man (Ming 後生 'junior') [兒子]
his, her, their (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]

sentences.t: Ečige-jin min-u žüġegsen na-da tügetele bijü.
sentences.l: Father's my put-by to-me enough is.
sentences.i: What my father laid by is quite enough for me.
sentences.n: ečige-jin min-u is 'my father's', the genitive -jin after a vowel with min-u set after it. žüġegsen is Ming 置來的, 'what has been put by' (stem žüġe- inferred) + the participle -gsen. na-da is 'to me', and tügetele is Ming 儘勾, 'fully enough' (the stem tüge- and the ending -tele are uncertain). bijü 'is'.

morph.gloss: my (genitive of bi, placed after its noun) [我的]
to put by, lay up (Ming 置來的; stem inferred) [置來的]
to suffice, be enough (Ming 儘勾; stem inferred) [儘勾]

sentences.t: Bi ülü abqu tusa boluγsan min-u jaγ̇un tusa bolqu; ülü abqu" keġebe.
sentences.l: I not take; use having-been my what use will-be; not take" said.
sentences.i: "I will not take it. What use would my help be if I took a share? I will not take it," he said.
sentences.n: Bi ülü abqu is 'I will not take (it)'. tusa boluγsan min-u is 'my having been of use' (Ming 濟 做來的 我的): bol- 'become' + the participle -uγsan + the genitive min-u. jaγ̇un tusa bolqu is 'what use will it be' (甚麽 濟 做), a rhetorical question. The Ming is clear but the whole is compressed; my English fills in 'if I took a share'. ülü abqu keġebe closes the quotation. The part ends with the refusal.

morph.gloss: past participle: what has been …-ed (Ming 做來的)
my (genitive of bi, placed after its noun) [我的]
